title: Lisse modules associated to compact continuous-function torsors
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Write $k=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ for its function field, choose a separable closure $k^s/k$ [def-pd-separable-closure], and put $G_k=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its profinite Krull topology. For any nonarchimedean normed field $A$ (a field with a multiplicative absolute value satisfying $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$), put $R_{A,T}=p_T^*\underline A$, where $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ for profinite $S$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. All module objects and lisse modules are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use all continuous functions with the norm topology. Assume further that $X$ is quasi-compact. Let $\bar\eta$ be the geometric generic point given by an algebraic closure containing $k^s$, put $\Pi_\eta=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar\eta)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor], and let $q:G_k\to\Pi_\eta$ be induced by $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$. Let $H$ be a compact Hausdorff topological group with a basis of identity neighborhoods consisting of open subgroups, $r:H\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ a continuous homomorphism for some $n\geq0$, and $\theta:\Pi_\eta\to H$ a continuous homomorphism. Let $(P,p)$ be a pointed right $F_H$-torsor of monodromy $\theta$ under [lem-sfb-complete-group-torsor-monodromy, def-sfb-continuous-right-torsor]. There exists a lisse $R_{A,X}$-module $L$ of rank $n$, canonically up to its pointed associated-module identification, locally glued from $R_A^n$ along $P$ by $r$: on a covering with sections $p_i$ and $p_j=p_i h_{ij}$, its corresponding frame identifications $e_i:R_A^n\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ obey $e_j=e_i\,r(h_{ij})$. Equivalently its associated-module relation is $[ph,v]=[p,r(h)v]$. Its underlying sheaf, addition and $R_A$-action all descend, and this construction is independent of the trivializing covering up to the indicated isomorphism. The point $p$ induces a basis of $V_A(L)$ in which its generic cocycle is
$$\sigma_L(g)=r(\theta(q(g)))\quad(g\in G_k).$$
If $F=\widehat A$ and $\iota:A\hookrightarrow F$ [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion], the frame torsor of $R_F\otimes_{R_A}L$ (a torsor under $F_{\operatorname{GL}_n(F)}$, the group $\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ satisfying the complete coefficient-group hypotheses by [lem-sfb-complete-nonarchimedean-matrix-group]) is the extension of $P$ along $\iota_*r:H\to\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$, with the induced point, and its generic cocycle is $\iota_*r\theta q$. In particular, for every continuous $\rho:\Pi_\eta\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$, its image $H=\rho(\Pi_\eta)$ with the subspace topology satisfies these hypotheses, and the associated module has generic cocycle $\rho q$.

proof.text: Work in compatible universes, taking a small model of the pro-etale site and a coefficient universe containing its objects, arrows and covering indices. Nonarchimedean balls separate distinct elements of $A$ by clopen sets: if $0<t<|a-b|$, the ball $|x-a|<t$ is open and its complement is open by the ultrametric inequality. Thus $A$ is totally disconnected. The continuous-field realization identifies $R_A(U)$ with $C(|U|,A)$ as rings. Use the internal/section-module equivalence with the sheafified tensor structure; these hypotheses hold for abelian sheaves on this small site. A homomorphism $R_A^n|_U\to R_A^m|_U$ is exactly a matrix over $R_A(U)$: its columns are the images of the standard basis sections, and their linear combinations define the inverse correspondence on every object over $U$. Hence its automorphisms are $C(|U|,\operatorname{GL}_n(A))$. Indeed the entries of a continuous matrix function are continuous; pointwise inversion is continuous by the adjugate/determinant formula and continuity of inversion in a normed field. Invertible matrices of continuous functions and continuous functions into invertible matrices are therefore the same. This includes empty matrices.

source.place: Lemma 7.4.7, frame-sheaf interpretation; continuous-function realization supplied by the cited node

proof.text: Choose a covering $U_i\to X$ with torsor sections $p_i$. The right-torsor axiom gives unique $h_{ij}\in C(|U_i\times_XU_j|,H)$ with $p_j=p_i h_{ij}$. Uniqueness gives $h_{ik}=h_{ij}h_{jk}$ on triple overlaps, including repeated indices. Postcomposition by the continuous homomorphism $r$ gives matrices $t_{ij}=r(h_{ij})$ over $R_A$, with $t_{ik}=t_{ij}t_{jk}$. Apply site module-sheaf gluing to the local modules $R_A^n$ and the coordinate-change isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}=t_{ij}^{-1}$, for which $\phi_{ik}=\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}$. If $a_i:L|_{U_i}\to R_A^n$ are the resulting identifications, put $e_i=a_i^{-1}$. Then $e_j=e_i t_{ij}$, with precisely the order claimed. The gluing theorem descends the module structure, hence the underlying abelian sheaf, addition and scalar action; the equivalence in step 1 gives the requested internal module. These local identifications make it lisse of rank $n$ by definition.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, with module operations; Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 7.4.7, descent construction

proof.text: For another local section $p'=ph$, define $e_{p'}=e_p r(h)$. This is independent of the chart: if $p=p_i a=p_j b$ then $a=h_{ij}b$, and $e_i r(a)=e_j r(b)$. It also gives $e_{ph}(v)=e_p(r(h)v)$, hence the relation $[ph,v]=[p,r(h)v]$. Conversely this relation reduces every locally represented pair to its unique vector in a chart. On a common refinement of two trivializing coverings, these formulas give linear isomorphisms between the two glued modules. They agree on double overlaps, so the map-gluing part of set-sheaf cover descent gives unique global maps. Their composites are identities because they are identities locally; linearity follows by the same local equality check. The same uniqueness gives the composition identity for three coverings. This proves the stated canonical independence relative to the associated-module identifications. It does not assert that a chosen basis alone kills every module automorphism.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps; the associated-module relation is the elementary local computation

proof.text: The integral scheme $X$ is connected, and locally Noetherian plus quasi-compact is Noetherian in the torsor correspondence. Restrict $(P,p)$ to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Pullback naturality and the field clause of the complete-group torsor correspondence give a section $p$ over $k^s$ whose Cech translation is $c(g)=\theta(q(g))$: $\mathrm{pr}_2^*p=\mathrm{pr}_1^*p\,c$. The continuous-set comparison is natural in the coefficient space, respects finite products and commutes with this inverse image. Module pullback sends the regular module to the regular module by $a\otimes b\mapsto a\alpha(b)$, inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, and is additive by its definition. It therefore preserves the finite free frames. Applying inverse image to the chart equations of steps 2--3 thus gives a frame $e_p:R_A^n\simeq L|_{k^s}$ with $e_{pc}=e_p r(c)$. The field Cech calculation identifies sections of this free module with $A^n$, so $p$ gives the asserted basis of $V_A(L)$. On the double overlap its two frames obey $e_2=e_1r(c)$. The generic cocycle $\sigma_L$ is, by its definition in the generic-cocycle lemma (whose hypotheses hold: $X$ is nonempty, connected, normal and Noetherian), the evaluated descent matrix over $\operatorname{Spec}k^s\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ in this basis; in the convention $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$ of the Cech calculation it is consequently $\sigma_L(g)=r(\theta(q(g)))$. The equation concerns frames, so no inverse has entered the displayed generic cocycle.

source.place: Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, with the field convention and pullback naturality explicitly supplied by the cited torsor and Cech nodes

proof.text: Let $F=\widehat A$ and $s=\iota_*r$. The completion lemma makes $\iota$ an isometric continuous field inclusion. Apply the generic lisse scalar-comparison lemma: $L_F=R_F\otimes_{R_A}L$ is lisse of rank $n$, the basis from $p$ extends to the basis $1\otimes e_p$, and transition matrices and generic cocycles are sent entrywise by $\iota$. Thus the local frames $e_{i,F}$ obey $e_{j,F}=e_{i,F}s(h_{ij})$, and the generic cocycle is $s\theta q$. By the matrix-group lemma $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ is Hausdorff, has an open-subgroup identity basis and is two-sided complete. The matrix calculation in step 1, now for the nonarchimedean field $F$, identifies the automorphisms of $R_F^n$ with $F_G$. Isomorphisms and their inverses glue by set-sheaf map descent, so the frame presheaf is a sheaf. Consequently the frame sheaf $Q$ of $L_F$ is a right $F_G$-torsor, with local section $e_{i,F}$ and right action by precomposition.

source.place: Lemma 7.4.7, frames and scalar extension; completion and entrywise scalar comparison are the separate cited inputs

proof.text: Identify this frame torsor with the extension of $P$ along $s$. The formula $(p,a)\mapsto e_{p,F}\circ a$ is natural and balanced, since $e_{ph,F}\circ a=e_{p,F}\circ s(h)a$. Locally, where $p=p_i h$, it is $(p_i h,a)\mapsto e_{i,F}s(h)a$. To verify the extension universal property, let $b:P\times F_G\to T$ be any balanced natural map to a set sheaf. On $U_i$ the only possible map $Q\to T$ is $e_{i,F}a\mapsto b(p_i,a)$. These maps agree on overlaps: $e_{j,F}a=e_{i,F}s(h_{ij})a$ and $b(p_j,a)=b(p_i,s(h_{ij})a)$. Set-sheaf map descent gives a unique global map. It factors $b$ by the local formula, and uniqueness is checked in the same charts. This is exactly the extension presentation of the right-torsor definition. Right equivariance is the equality $(e_{p,F}a)b=e_{p,F}(ab)$; its induced fibre point is $e_{p,F}$, the extended basis. Together with step 5 this proves both the completed frame identification and its pointed generic cocycle.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps; universal property computed in torsor charts

proof.text: Finally let $\rho:\Pi_\eta\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ be continuous and give $H=\rho(\Pi_\eta)$ the subspace topology. The automorphism-profinite lemma applied to the finite-set fibre functor makes $\Pi_\eta$ compact. Its continuous image $H$ is compact: pull any open cover back to the compact source and push the resulting finite subcover forward. It is Hausdorff as a subspace of the finite matrix space over the normed field $A$. The isometry $A\hookrightarrow F$ embeds finite matrix spaces and hence $\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ topologically into $\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$. Intersecting the open subgroups $U_t$ of the completed matrix-group lemma with $H$ gives an identity-neighborhood basis of open subgroups of $H$: intersections are subgroups and openness and the basis property follow directly from the subspace topology. The map $\theta:\Pi_\eta\to H$ obtained by restricting the codomain of $\rho$ is continuous, and the inclusion $r:H\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ is a continuous homomorphism with $r\theta=\rho$. The compact case of the torsor correspondence supplies its pointed torsor; steps 2--4 apply and give $\sigma_L=\rho q$. If $n=0$, all matrices and groups here are trivial, the glued module and both vector spaces are zero, and the same formulas still apply.
